findings.evidence: pnpm test:infra builds jade-app:ci, and image.test.ts checks that image. But compose-up.test.ts brings the stack up with an env file from env:init that has no JADE_IMAGE, and D2 gives app and migrate `image: ${JADE_IMAGE:-jade-app:local}` with `build: .`. So the stack tests build and run a second image, jade-app:local, instead of the one image.test.ts checked. Z3 says the image job pushes 'the image it tested', yet the image proven through Caddy and migrate is not the one pushed. Unless buildx's cache is shared, the second build also adds time that the 6:15 image-job estimate in 12.2 does not include.
findings.fix: Have the infra tests and the image job run the stack with JADE_IMAGE=jade-app:ci and without a build (`up --no-build`, or `pull_policy: never` in the test override). Assert in compose-up.test.ts that the running app container's image ID equals the one image.test.ts inspected, and in ci-workflow.test.ts that the image job passes JADE_IMAGE.
findings.path: section 11 checks (compose-up, caddy-logs, media) and D2; section 14 Z3

findings.evidence: In CI, MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL carries the service container's test-only owner password (X2, V5 ci profile), and V2 refuses any test-only value unless APP_ENV is test. So `db:reset` under APP_ENV=production exits non-zero with a ConfigError before U6's own guard (APP_ENV development or test, loopback host) ever runs. The test passes in the required CI job even if that guard were missing. The guard is tested only by local gates, where the generated passwords carry no marker.
findings.fix: Make the production case assert U6's own refusal (a fixed tag such as DB_RESET_REFUSED, checked before any connection), with URLs that pass V2 under production: generated non-marker passwords, in the style of V8. Add a case with a non-loopback host under APP_ENV=test, so both halves of the guard are proven in CI.
findings.path: section 9 checks, tests/integration/db-scripts.test.ts ('reset under APP_ENV=production exits non-zero and changes nothing'); V2; X2

findings.evidence: D1 sets `USER node` (uid 1000), and Z2 runs `docker run --rm` with the env directory mounted to write the VM's env file, mode 600. The file is then owned by uid 1000. If the VM's non-root deploy user (Z1) has a different uid, Compose run as that user cannot read its own project .env, and the first deploy fails. Nothing in Z2 or the rehearsal sets or checks the file's owner.
findings.fix: Run the container with `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` of the deploy user, or chown the file afterwards in the deploy-user script. Add a check to the deploy/staging scripts or the local rehearsal that the env file is owned by the deploy user and has mode 600.
